Mr. Anuj Kumar, Advocat  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AMIT SHARMA  ORDER % 18.01.2023 CRL.M.A. 1276/2023 (Exemption) Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

The application is disposed of accordingly.
W.P.(CRL) 138/2023

The present petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeks quashing of FIR No. 153/2019, under Sections 498A/406/506/34 IPC, registered at P.S. Khajuri Khas, Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
The marriage between petitioner no.1/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 19.06.2017 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.
Due to temperamental differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately from 22.04.2018.

sentences.text:
Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged an FIR against petitioner no.1 (husband),
petitioner no. 2 (father-in-law), petitioner no. 3 (mother-in-law), petitioner no.4 (sister-in-law),
petitioner no.5 (sister-in- law) & petitioner no.6 (uncle of husband).

On 24.09.2022, parties arrived at a settlement before Counselling Cell, Family Courts, Delhi and as per the said settlement/agreement, petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay an amount of Rs. 6,90,000/- to the respondent no.2/wife towards full and final settlement of all her claims including istridhan,
permanent alimony and maintenance - present, past and future.
The copy of the aforesaid settlement/agreement dated 24.09.2022 is on record (Annexure P-4).

In terms of the said settlement, the marriage between the parties stands dissolved by a decree of divorce dated 24.12.2022, passed by Mr. Ankur Jain, Judge, Family Court, North-East,
Karkardooma Courts, Delhi, (Annexure P-5).

sentences.text:
Further, as per the settlement/agreement, an amount of Rs. 4,60,000/- has already been paid to respondent no.2 and the remaining amount of Rs.
2,30,000/- has been paid to her in court today, by means of a demand draft.

Petitioners and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and have been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer, ASI B.D. Sharma, P.S.
Khajuri Khas, Delhi.
A demand draft bearing no. 325175 dated 12.01.2023 for Rs. 2,30,000/- drawn on Central Bank of India has been handed over complainant/Respondent No.2, who acknowledges the receipt of the same.
The complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
She further states that all the terms of the agreement have been complied with.
In view of the settlement between the parties, learned ASC for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, the Honble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-
"61. ...

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceedings or continuation of criminal proceedings would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."

In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 153/2019, under Manmohan Singh & Ors vs The State (Gnct Of Delhi) & Anr on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158023684/
2 Sections 498A/406/506/34 IPC, registered at P.S. Khajuri Khas, Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 153/2019, under Sections 498A/406/506/34 IPC, registered at P.S. Khajuri Khas, Delhi and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, is hereby quashed.
